newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche hits back at critics over Krupp.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche hits back at critics over Krupp.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG on Monday hit back against accusations it had engaged in "Wild West" tactics in supporting Krupp AG's takeover bid for Thyssen AG and reiterated it was not pursuing any industrial policy of its own.
"Talk by some politicians and trade unionists of conspiracy theories, Wild West manners, and claims to power by banks, lacks any foundation," Deutsche said in a press statement.

The bank said that all it had done was to accept a mandate to advise a company on the arranging and financing of a takeover bid. This was a common practice both nationally and internationally, it said.

Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp launched the bid last Tuesday but it was shelved on Wednesday for eight days of talks on a possible uncontested merger. If the talks fail, Krupp has said it will go ahead with the takeover.

"Deutsche Bank did not link any self-interest on economic policy by taking on the mandate from Krupp," the statement said. "Deutsche Bank repeats that it fundamentally does not pursue its own industrial policy."
But the statement added that Deutsche was prepared to cooperate in implementing such a policy if it appeared to make economic sense.

"Like all interested parties Deutsche Bank believes that only a rapid reorganisation of the German steel industry will lead to safer jobs in the long term. Germany must remain a steel location! Deutsche Bank will go along with any promising concept that leads to this."
